official.deadline_note: Financial aid document deadlines follow the admission round: Nov 15 (Early Action, Early Decision I and QuestBridge), Jan 15 (Early Decision II), Feb 15 (Regular Decision); if a deadline falls on a weekend or holiday it moves to the next business day. Admission application deadlines are Nov 2, 2026 (EA/ED I) and Jan 4, 2027 (ED II and Regular Decision). Transfer applicants must indicate interest in need-based aid before being admitted (transfer aid deadlines March 15 for transfer Early Decision and April 1 for transfer Rolling Decision), but international transfer students are not eligible for aid.
official.application_cycle: Fall 2027 entry cycle; applications for the current entry round are open, and the published cost figures are for 2026-27
official.status_note: The College is accepting applications for the current entry cycle and the Office of Financial Aid lists this cycle's aid document deadlines of Nov 15, Jan 15 and Feb 15 by admission round, noting that students who submit financial aid requirements after the deadline will not be eligible to apply.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Need-based gift aid from the College is intended to cover tuition and fees as much as possible, and packages are built from an estimate of the full costs of enrolling at the University of Chicago, including tuition, housing, health insurance, a meal plan, and estimates for additional costs like books and personal expenses; UChicago states it is committed to meeting 100% of demonstrated need with a loan-free package for admitted students who applied for funding.

official.citizenship_residency: Neither a U.S. citizen nor a U.S. permanent resident, regardless of where in the world you live and go to school

official.duration: Aid is determined during the admissions process prior to the first year and is re-applied for in each subsequent year of the College
official.description: The College welcomes talented students from around the world and is dedicated to providing financial support regardless of home address: admitted international first-year applicants who applied for funding during admissions receive a loan-free package that meets 100% of demonstrated need, sized from the full estimated cost of enrolling, and all first-year applicants are also automatically considered for partial-tuition merit scholarships.
official.program_type: Need-based loan-free institutional financial aid for international undergraduates, plus partial-tuition merit scholarships
official.english_requirement: No minimum score is published: UChicago only admits students who have demonstrated a superior level of English language competence, and students are invited but not required to submit scores from any English proficiency examination, with official or self-reported scores accepted (official reports only if admitted and enrolling); UChicago does not offer an ESL program for admitted students

verification.notes: All values were read live from uchicago.edu pages on 2026-10-10; the brief's official_source_url (uchicago.edu/admissions/undergraduate/financial-aid/international-students) returns 404 and was replaced by the live College Admissions international financial aid page. No fixed award figure is published: aid equals 100% of demonstrated need, loan-free, and is 'sometimes up to the cost of attendance' (2026-27 on-campus total $103,821), so funding_amount is null. The Office of Financial Aid states that expenses beyond tuition and fees are paid out of pocket or through the international student stipend, so fully_funded is recorded as false even though the catalogue labels the item Fully Funded.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a standalone scholarship you apply for: it is UChicago's institutional aid system for admitted international first-years, and the one decision that matters is whether you apply for aid when you submit your admission application. If you do and are admitted, UChicago builds a loan-free package sized to your family's documented income and assets, up to the full cost of attendance ($103,821 on campus in 2026-27), with tuition and fees covered by gift aid and food, housing and any travel handled through a stipend paid directly to you. Aid is re-applied for each year, so the package can follow you through all four years of the College. Merit scholarships exist but are partial-tuition, decided independently of need, and only winners ever hear back.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First-year international applicants whose families cannot meet a roughly $104k annual bill and who can produce translated tax, income and asset documents before their admission round's aid deadline.
application_readiness_checklist: Decide before submitting the admission application whether you are applying for aid, because applying afterwards is impossible
Gather the most recent completed tax year's forms for both parents, plus bank, investment and property statements, or employer and bank-statement evidence if your country does not require tax filing
Arrange certified English translations of every non-English document and convert amounts to U.S. Dollars in advance
Create the UChicago Account early and work through its document checklist, uploading everything there since emailed documents are not accepted
Work backwards from your round's aid document deadline (Nov 15, Jan 15 or Feb 15), which is later than but separate from the admission deadline
common_rejection_risks: Applying for aid only after the admission decision arrives, since UChicago states those students cannot apply in later years
Filing the CSS Profile, the FAFSA or IDOC documents and assuming the aid file is therefore complete
Missing the aid document deadline for the chosen round, which the Office of Financial Aid warns voids eligibility
Leaving assets undocumented, such as a second property or an investment account, which stalls or shrinks the need analysis
Counting on a merit scholarship to make the numbers work, when UChicago says the vast majority of its aid is need-based
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Gift aid targets tuition and fees, so plan for food and housing, travel to and from Chicago, books and personal expenses if the stipend does not stretch that far; health insurance sits outside the published cost-of-attendance figures, the $702 travel allowance is an estimate rather than a separate stipend, and first-time 2026 enrollees owe a $720 class fee in each of their first two years.
document_audit: Tax-year mismatch: the Office of Financial Aid's international page asks for 2025 forms while College Admissions still says 2024, so upload the most recent completed year and label it clearly
Home-country documents must be translated into English and converted into U.S. Dollars; untranslated originals slow the file down
There is no Proof of Family Income form, so choose deliberately between employer statements and bank statements showing recurring salary deposits when no tax filing is required
Asset verification covers all checking, savings and investment balances plus any property other than the primary home; omitting a small account is a common trap
alerts: Aid eligibility is decided once, at admission; there is no second chance in any later year of the College
International transfer students receive no need-based aid and no merit scholarships, and UChicago confirms there are no exceptions
Merit winners are notified on a rolling basis through the end of April, so silence means no award rather than a late one
If a deadline lands on a weekend or holiday it shifts to the next business day
Applying for need-based aid removes the $90 application fee entirely, so aid applicants pay nothing to apply
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application first through the Common Application or Apply Coalition, then the UChicago Financial Aid Worksheet and uploads inside the UChicago Account, with the aid decision reviewed case by case alongside the chosen admission round.
